messages:
jamie: FYI hit a weird one in the python quickstart (FastAPI) where req_id is present in debug logs but redacted at info.

arjun: can you paste the log snippet and minimal repro steps?

jamie: steps: clone github.com/redwood/sample-apps/python-telemetry, pip install -r requirements.txt, export LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG, uvicorn app:app --reload, POST /session. Logs: 
```
INFO:     127.0.0.1:54321 - "POST /session HTTP/1.1" 200 OK
DEBUG: app.auth: parsed token - request_id=
DEBUG: uvicorn.access: 127.0.0.1 - "POST /session" 200 - request_id=xyz-999
INFO: app.handlers: session.created - request_id=REDACTED
```
looks like uvicorn.access logs (debug) are including a request_id that our redaction middleware hasn't touched. At INFO level the app.handlers message is redacted normally.

rachel: interesting — are you using structlog + standard logging adapters? We've seen uvicorn attach its own handler which doesn't go through our redaction filter.

jamie: yes app uses structlog.bind(request_id=...) in middleware after parsing headers. The redaction filter is a logging.Filter attached to the root logger. But uvicorn creates its own logger and adds a StreamHandler before middleware runs in reload mode.

arjun: so order: uvicorn logging handler emits early debug logs (including request_id if present in contextvars), then our middleware binds request_id to structlog later. If the handler doesn't apply our redaction filter, it prints raw.

jamie: exactly. I tested adding our redaction filter to "uvicorn.access" in the quickstart and that fixed it. Also reproduced by forcing LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG which enables extra debug statements from third-party libs that circumvent our handler chain.

rachel: two mitigations: 1) ensure sampleapp attaches the global redaction filter to the uvicorn/uvicorn.access loggers on startup, 2) update SDK to provide a small helper that registers the redaction filter to common external loggers (uvicorn, gunicorn, aiohttp). The helper could be idempotent and called during SDK init.

arjun: I prefer we ship both: patch quickstart + a tiny SDK utility register_redaction_for_known_loggers(). Also document in onboarding: "If using uvicorn/gunicorn, call telemetry.init() before starting server or configure server logging to propagate to root logger."

jamie: filed a repro branch and a draft PR to sample-apps with test that starts uvicorn programmatically and asserts logs don't contain unredacted tokens even at DEBUG.

ci-bot: CI check started for PR #348 — running python/telemetry quickstart tests.

rachel: also double-check structlog config: when structlog config is applied after uvicorn adds handlers, you can end up with duplicate messages. Suggest move telemetry.init() into app startup event so handlers are consistent across reloads.

arjun: good call. Add a note about --reload dev mode because reload spins up a child process with its own logging setup; that was why this was flaky locally.

telemetry-bot: Created issue https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/issues/1493 — "Python quickstart: uvicorn handler bypasses redaction at DEBUG; add SDK helper and onboarding doc note" Labels: devex, telemetry, bug.

jamie: I'll update the PR to call register_redaction_for_known_loggers() during init and add a small smoke test for --reload. Thanks all :raised_hands:
